payload.title: Publish go-diffutils' modules
payload.description: Publish go-diffutils' modules: settle its git and license state, add CI and a Release workflow, and ready each module for its first tag
payload.context:
Found 2026-10-26 while planning go-tealeaves E-2440 (from go-dt E-2431's session). go-tealeaves' teadiff module and several example modules require github.com/mikeschinkel/go-diffutils through `replace => ../go-diffutils`, so no go-tealeaves module builds for anyone but Mike, and E-2440 (no replace in publishable modules) cannot finish until go-diffutils is published. Mike asked for one task covering everything go-diffutils needs, not several.

State on 2026-10-26:
- The checkout is mid-rebase. Mike made a local initial commit (e05e63c), created the GitHub repo, which made its own initial commit (a2092d0: LICENSE and README.md), and pulling it conflicted in LICENSE. `git status` shows an interactive rebase of e05e63c onto a2092d0 stopped on that conflict, with every other file staged.
- Three modules: root (github.com/mikeschinkel/go-diffutils), dmp and sgdiff. dmp and sgdiff each require the root at v0.0.0 through `replace => ../`. No tags exist, no .github workflows, no justfile.
- Licensing. difflib.go holds code absorbed from github.com/pmezard/go-difflib, Copyright (c) 2013 Patrick Mezard, under the BSD 2-Clause license; its source keeps that copyright line. The local LICENSE is Mike's MIT license with the go-difflib notice and BSD 2-Clause text appended. dmp and sgdiff only import sergi/go-diff and sourcegraph/go-diff as module dependencies; no code from them is copied in. Mike intends MIT for his own code, is unsure how to credit absorbed BSD code within or beside a standard license, would switch the package to BSD 2-Clause if needed for compatibility, and wants help deciding.

Mike's words on scope: resolve all of go-diffutils' issues, add .github workflows, and publish released versions, ideally as one task. go-dt E-2431 is the model for a multi-module repo: no replace in publishable modules, an uncommitted generated go.work (`just work`), CI with GOWORK=off, and a Release workflow taking a module choice and making directory-prefixed tags (dmp/vX.Y.Z). The user makes the tags by running the workflow.

payload.title: Keep the root release marked latest after nested releases
payload.description: Keep the root release marked latest: pass make_latest to action-gh-release in go-diffutils' and go-dt's release.yml, true for root and false for nested modules
payload.context: Found 2026-10-27 after E-2449's first releases: Mike ran Release for root, dmp, then sgdiff, and GitHub marked sgdiff/v0.1.0 as latest because it was created last. He would rather root stay latest, and would otherwise have to set it by hand after every nested release. softprops/action-gh-release@v2 takes a make_latest input. go-dt's release.yml, the model for go-diffutils', has the same gap. Mike also wants this eventually built into Gomion as an automated release step.

fields.title: Bring go-pkgs CI and Release workflows to go-dt's model
fields.description: Bring every go-pkgs repo's CI and Release workflows to go-dt's model, fixing the model as it goes: module choice, prefixed tags, publishability checks, .endless-free root notes, root kept latest, and no Actions warnings or notices
fields.context:
Mike chose this on 2026-10-27 while planning go-dt E-2452, which leaves commits touching only .endless/ out of go-dt's root release notes. 12 go-pkgs repos have a release.yml and 16 use Endless, so every repo with both lists Endless's auto-commits in its root release notes, as go-dt's v0.6.1 did (41 commits listed, 3 of them real changes). An Endless task lands only in its own project, so E-2452 fixes go-dt alone. Mike picked one Gomion task covering every repo, so each gets the .endless exclusion together with the rest of go-dt's E-2431 release.yml: a module input (root plus nested modules), vX.Y.Z for root and <dir>/vX.Y.Z for nested modules, refusal of a wrong module path, a replace directive or an existing tag, tests with GOWORK=off, and per-module previous tags and notes. ED-1639 (accepted) sets the no-replace rule the workflow enforces. Gomion is Mike's tool for managing Go package versions; whether this becomes a Gomion command that writes or checks release.yml, or a one-off change across repos, is for the plan to settle.

Widened on 2026-10-27 after go-diffutils E-2449's first releases (Mike chose to widen this task rather than file another; E-2458, filed in go-diffutils by mistake, is obsolete in its favour). The model go-dt and go-diffutils share has gaps of its own, so this task covers CI (test.yml) as well as Release, fixing the model as it rolls it out:

- Keep root marked latest. GitHub marks the release created last as latest, so releasing root, then dmp, then sgdiff left sgdiff/v0.1.0 marked latest. softprops/action-gh-release@v2 takes make_latest: true for root, false for nested modules. Mike would otherwise have to set it by hand after every nested release, and wants it automated in Gomion eventually.
- Eliminate every Actions warning and notice. Mike's rule: warnings and notices are removed wherever possible, never accepted as informational, so a new one gets attention. go-diffutils' Test run 40492343066 (10 warnings, 5 notices) and Release run 40492576617 (4 warnings, 3 notices) show three causes, which go-dt most likely shares:
  1. Node.js 20 deprecation, once per job: actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-go@v5, actions/cache@v4 and softprops/action-gh-release@v2 target Node 20 and are forced onto Node 24. Fix: move each to a release that targets Node 24.
  2. "Restore cache failed: Dependencies file is not found ... go.sum" from setup-go's built-in cache: it looks for go.sum at the repo root, and a root module with no dependencies has none. The workflows already cache with actions/cache, so setup-go's cache is redundant there. Fix: cache: false, or cache-dependency-path: '**/go.sum'.
  3. "The ubuntu-latest label will migrate to Ubuntu 26", once per job. Fix: name a pinned runner image instead of ubuntu-latest.

fields.reason: Filed in the wrong project: release-workflow work for go-pkgs repos belongs to gomion. Folded into gomion's E-2454, widened to cover it; no command exists yet to move a task between projects (E-2459).

payload.title: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows
payload.description: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows in go-diffutils by running gomion repo setup, committing the result, and confirming the first Actions runs show no warnings or notices
payload.plan:
# Plan: adopt gomion's generated workflows in go-diffutils

1. Use a gomion build that includes E-2454's `gomion repo` commands.
2. In go-diffutils, run `gomion repo setup`. It raises each go.mod below Go 1.27 and tidies it, then writes .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml.
3. Run `gomion repo setup --check`; it must report the repo up to date.
4. Run each module's tests locally with GOWORK=off.
5. Commit the generated workflows and the raised go.mod/go.sum files together.

After the land: push, then read the annotations on the first Test run (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` for each job), and on the next Release run once there is one. Each must show zero warnings and zero notices; any that remain are fixed in gomion's templates, not here.

ops.statement: go-diffutils's .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml are exactly what gomion repo workflows generates, and gomion repo setup --check reports the repo up to date
Every go.mod in go-diffutils declares go 1.27 or later and is tidy
Does not hand-edit the generated workflow files; a change goes into gomion's templates
After the push, the first Test run and the next Release run show zero Actions warnings and zero notices

payload.title: Prepare go-diffutils for a tagged release
payload.description: Prepare go-diffutils for release by committing and pushing pending work, then propose a version and description per module for the owner to tag.
payload.plan:
## Plan
1. Run `git status` and `git log <latest-tag>..HEAD` in the go-diffutils repo; list every module in it that has its own go.mod and tag prefix.
2. Commit any uncommitted work that belongs in the release. Ask the owner about anything unclear instead of guessing.
3. Run the repo's build, vet and tests. Fix or report any failure.
4. Push main to origin. Do not create or push tags.
5. For each module, compare the changes since its latest tag and propose a semver version, explaining whether the change is breaking.
6. Draft a release description for each module.
7. Report the proposed versions and descriptions to the owner. The owner tags and releases when ready.
payload.context: gomion cannot drop its local replace directive for go-diffutils until its work is committed, pushed and tagged on GitHub.

payload.title: Add ChangeBlockSummary and SummarizeChangeBlocks
payload.description: Add ChangeBlockSummary, a shortened view of one change block (type, line count, context before and after, changed lines, truncated), and SummarizeChangeBlocks(*DiffContent) []ChangeBlockSummary.
payload.context: Two packages hold their own copy of the same block-summary types. gomion's gomtui has CondensedBlock and FileCondensedDiff in context_info_pane_model.go, built by BuildCondensedDiff from gomion's internal gitutils.FileChanges. go-tealeaves' teadiff copied CondensedBlock, FileDiff and FileStatus into teadiff/types.go. The builder reads only old and new lines plus each change's type and line ranges, which DiffContent already carries, and it uses neither git nor a TUI, so go-diffutils is its home. go-gitutil's FileChanges.ToDiffContent already converts to DiffContent. A go-gitutil planning document (PLAN-CONDENSED-DIFF-TYPES.md, removed by go-gitutil's release task) had proposed go-gitutil as the home.
payload.analysis: Decided with Mike on 2026-11-16, in go-gitutil E-2624's session: the type is named ChangeBlockSummary because 'Condensed' did not say what the type represents. go-diffutils adds no per-file wrapper: teadiff keeps FileDiff (path, status, blocks) as its render input, since DiffContent's Label already carries the path and status is a rendering concern. The behaviour to carry over from gomtui's BuildCondensedDiff: added blocks read NewLines over NewRange and deleted blocks read OldLines over OldRange; up to 2 context lines before and after; all changed lines when there are 5 or fewer, otherwise the first 3 with the truncated flag set.
